verdict.rationale: Open WebUI is documented as a self-hosted platform built to run entirely offline, with local models via Ollama and an air-gapped deployment option. Keeping data on your own infrastructure this way effectively stops it from reaching third parties who could train on it. The guarantee is architectural only, though: the docs never state a no-training policy, and when users connect cloud OpenAI-compatible providers, their data goes to those providers under the providers' terms. Missing for 10: an explicit statement that Open WebUI does not train on user data, any per-provider training opt-out control or guidance, and independent corroboration of the privacy posture.
